lecture_11.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 11: Scaling - case study and details
lecture_11.anchor_convention: lecture_11.pdf:p<page>, page numbers from `pdftotext -layout` form feeds (title slide = p1; 58 content pages, p59 empty)
lecture_11.note: Evidence is the text layer of the slides (lecture_11.txt), split page-by-page by discover_slides.py into discovered.json. The deck is a case-study tour of published scaling recipes (MiniCPM, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi K2, Hunyuan, LLaMA 3, MiniMax-01, StepFun, CerebrasGPT) followed by a derivation of muP and a replication of its robustness; nearly every quantitative result (optimal-LR curves, batch-vs-loss fits, WSD loss curves, IsoFLOP parabolas, fitted ratios other than 96-1 and 39-1, Muon speedrun gains, CerebrasGPT curves, muP replication sweeps, RMSNorm-gain and weight-decay failures) is a screenshot whose numbers are not in the text layer. Each KP's filtering_note says when a number is figure-only. The muP derivation on p46-p50 is mangled by layout extraction (stacked fractions, square roots and norm bars are lost; see `dropped` in discovered.json); KPs quote the surviving ASCII text verbatim and state the reconstructed formula.

lecture_02.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 2: Resource accounting
lecture_02.note: Referenced only through external_prerequisites (lecture_02:six-nd); see atlas/lectures/lecture_02/knowledge_points.json. minicpm_2024.title: MiniCPM: Unveiling the Potential of Small Language Models with Scalable Training Strategies (Hu et al., 2024)
minicpm_2024.note: p5-p18: 'MiniCPM (2024) - small, high-perf LM from Tsinghua group'. Source of the muP hyperparameters printed on p8 (scale_emb = 12, scale_depth = 1.4, init_std = 0.1, lr = 0.01), the optimal-batch sweep over 9m/30m/170m models (p11), the WSD schedule (p14-p15) and the Chinchilla method 1 + method 3 analysis (p16-p18). The deck names the model, not the paper; identification is the atlas author's (the printed hyperparameters match the paper's Table).

deepseek_llm_2024.title: DeepSeek LLM: Scaling Open-Source Language Models with Longtermism (DeepSeek-AI, 2024)
deepseek_llm_2024.note: p19-p24: 7B and 67B models; batch/LR fitted directly as functions of compute without muP ('near optimal' = within 0.25% of the minimum loss, p21); multi-step (WSD-style) schedule with two 10% decay steps (p22); IsoFLOP (Chinchilla method 2) model-size analysis (p23) and the loss prediction check (p24). Deck names the model, not the paper.

hoffmann_2022.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Hoffmann et al., 2022; 'Chinchilla')
hoffmann_2022.note: The 'chinchilla' of p2, p13, p16-p18, p23, p40, p45. Methods 1 (lower envelope), 2 (IsoFLOP) and 3 (joint fit) are named by number on p16-p18 and p23 and are defined in lecture_09:chinchilla-three-methods. Spelled 'Chinchlla' on p17.

kaplan_2020.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models (Kaplan et al., 2020)
kaplan_2020.note: p12: 'follow the Kaplan 2020 analysis and plot optimal batch size vs final loss'. Also the 'OpenAI' view of p33 (critical batch as a function of loss), together with McCandlish et al. 2018.

mccandlish_2018.title: An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training (McCandlish, Kaplan, Amodei, 2018)
mccandlish_2018.note: p33: 'Critical batch: batch as a function of loss (OpenAI)'. The deck does not name the paper; identification follows lecture_09:critical-batch-size.

qwen25_2024.title: Qwen2.5 Technical Report (Qwen Team, 2024)
qwen25_2024.note: p25: 'Qwen 2.5 - batch and hyper scaling fits'; p30: 'Qwen - Lr/batch (very few details..)'. Figure only.

qwen3_2025.title: Qwen3 Technical Report (Qwen Team, 2025)
qwen3_2025.note: p25: 'Qwen 3 - similar scaling for LR/batch'. Figure only.

kimi_k2_2025.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence (Kimi Team, 2025)
kimi_k2_2025.note: p26: 'sparsity scaling law to find the right sparsity levels'; p43: Kimi K2 as the large-scale evidence that Muon works. Figures only.

hunyuan_large_2024.title: Hunyuan-Large: An Open-Source MoE Model with 52 Billion Activated Parameters by Tencent (Sun et al., 2024)
hunyuan_large_2024.note: p27: 'Hunyuan (2024) large scaling laws' - IsoFLOP scaling for MoE active-parameter sizes, printed optimal ratio 96-1 (data to active param).

llama3_2024.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models (Grattafiori et al., 2024)
llama3_2024.note: p28: IsoFLOP scaling with printed 39-1 ratio, plus compute-to-downstream scaling (figure only).

minimax01_2025.title: MiniMax-01: Scaling Foundation Models with Lightning Attention (MiniMax, 2025)
minimax01_2025.note: p29: 'Architecture scaling laws + Chinchilla method 1'; p30: 'Architecture choice / decision scaling'. Figures only.

stepfun_step_law_2025.title: Predictable Scale: Part I - Optimal Hyperparameter Scaling Law in Large Language Model Pretraining (Li et al., StepFun, 2025)
stepfun_step_law_2025.note: p32-p37: 'Large scale scaling law study from StepFun' - grid search over LR/batch, convexity of loss in LR/batch (p35), batch depending primarily on dataset size and optimal LR rising with D at fixed M (p36), robustness to MoEs and other datasets (p37). The deck names the lab, not the paper; identification is the atlas author's.

zhou_2026.title: InternLM scaling law paper (Zhou+ 2026), cited on p36
zhou_2026.note: Only the string 'InternLM scaling law paper (Zhou+ 2026)' appears in the text layer; the deck gives no title or link, so the exact paper is not identified here. Cited for the claim that the optimal-LR-rises-with-D trend 'is likely more fragile if swapping to WSD'.

held_delphi_blog.title: William Held, 'delphi' blog post (oa.williamheld.com)
held_delphi_blog.note: p41: the only URL in the text layer. Source of the 'a good looking scaling can blow up' example (Cautious AdamC + sqrt batch-size scaling of learning rates), later 'fixed with some more careful parametrization / scaling / optimizer changes'.

muon_2024.title: Muon: An optimizer for hidden layers in neural networks (Keller Jordan et al., 2024, blog) and Muon is Scalable for LLM Training (Liu et al., Moonshot, 2025)
muon_2024.note: p42-p43: Muon as an optimizer for matrix-valued parameters whose Newton-Schulz iteration approximately orthogonalizes the update (U S V^T -> U V^T); the NanoGPT speedrun, a scaling study and Kimi K2 are shown as evidence. The deck names neither document; the blog is the original description and the Moonshot paper is the 'scaling study' most likely shown (inference).

cerebras_gpt_2023.title: Cerebras-GPT: Open Compute-Optimal Language Models Trained on the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Cluster (Dey et al., 2023)
cerebras_gpt_2023.note: p45: '0.1 to 13B models trained with the Chinchilla recipe', core finding that muP makes scaling more stable. Curves are figure only.

yang_2022.title: Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer (Yang et al., 2022; muP / muTransfer)
yang_2022.note: The 'maximum update parametrization' of p44-p57. The deck's derivation (p46-p50) follows an unnamed 'very accessible muP for babies paper' rather than this one; the per-layer table on p51 (embedding, attention params, input/output MLP, softmax linear) is a figure. Also the source of lecture_09:mup-scale-aware-lr.

mup_for_babies.title: 'muP for babies' paper (unnamed on p46)
mup_for_babies.note: p46 says only '(this is a very accessible muP for babies paper)' next to a screenshot. The spectral-norm derivation on p47-p49 (operator norm sqrt(n_{l-1}) + sqrt(n_l), condition on ||Delta W||_* sqrt(n_{l-1}) = Theta(sqrt(n_l))) matches Yang, Simon & Bernstein, 'A Spectral Condition for Feature Learning' (2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.17813), which the text layer does not say; slide image audit: p46's screenshot shows that title and its authors, so the identification is on the slide.

lion_2023.title: Symbolic Discovery of Optimization Algorithms (Chen et al., 2023; 'Lion')
lion_2023.note: p53 lists 'Exotic optimizers (Lion)' among components that deviate from muP's theory; p55 calls these 'exotic optimizers based on just gradient signs'. Named only as 'Lion' in the text layer.

mup_replication_unnamed.title: muP replication study behind p52-p57 ('Replicating muP', 'In our arch')
mup_replication_unnamed.note: p52-p57 report a replication (optimal LR vs width, robustness to SwiGLU/squared ReLU, batch size, zero-attention init, RMSNorm gains, Lion, regularizers; failures for RMSNorm gains and 0.1 weight decay). The text layer gives no title, author or link ('In our arch' on p54 suggests the lecturer's own group). Spoken (1:12:43-1:13:28): the lecturer attributes it to 'an independent researcher' ('he found'), so 'In our arch' is the paper's phrase, not the lecturer's group. A likely match is Lingle 2024 (arXiv:2404.05728, an independent researcher's muP learning-rate transfer study). Slide image audit: p51's image names it, Lucas Dax Lingle, 'A Large-Scale Exploration of μ-Transfer', and p52-p57 print its tables (optimal base LR per width, with ✔/✗ transfer marks: ✗ for RMSNorm gains, Lion and decoupled weight decay).
